\chapter{How Do You Say It?}
\label{ch:hi-how-do-you-say-it}
\hlchaptermodality{111}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask how to say something in Hindi, ask to be shown or to have it written down, and say I could not hear.}

Complete HI-C111-likh-dijie: a learner's toolkit of questions.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[hindī meṁ]{\hi{हिंदी} \hi{में} (hindī meṁ) — in Hindi}

\label{lesson:HI-C111-hindime}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for please wait, then the Hindi for meaning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हिंदी} \hi{में}}
\textbf{\hi{हिंदी} \hi{में}} (\emph{hindī meṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}in Hindi\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\hi{में}}, \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{}, the word you met on \textbf{\hi{रहना}}, after the name of the language. \textbf{\hi{अंग्रेज़ी} \hi{में}} — \textquotedblleft{}in English\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to name the language you want an answer in.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hindī meṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hindī meṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{hindī meṁ}, then \emph{aṅgrezī meṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for please wait, then the Hindi for meaning, then say \emph{hindī meṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{हिंदी} \hi{में} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}In Hindi\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kaise kahte haiṁ?]{\hi{कैसे} \hi{कहते} \hi{हैं}? (kaise kahte haiṁ?) — how do you say it?}

\label{lesson:HI-C111-kaisekahte}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for meaning, then the Hindi for in Hindi.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{कैसे} \hi{कहते} \hi{हैं}?}
\textbf{\hi{कैसे} \hi{कहते} \hi{हैं}?} (\emph{kaise kahte haiṁ?}) — \textquotedblleft{}how does one say it?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{हिंदी} \hi{में} 'book' \hi{कैसे} \hi{कहते} \hi{हैं}?} — \textquotedblleft{}how do you say 'book' in Hindi?\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{कहना}} is \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The one question that lets you learn from anyone.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaise kahte haiṁ?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaise kahte haiṁ?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{hindī meṁ 'book' kaise kahte haiṁ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for meaning, then the Hindi for in Hindi, then say \emph{kaise kahte haiṁ?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{कैसे} \hi{कहते} \hi{हैं}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}How do you say it?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dikhāie]{\hi{दिखाइए} (dikhāie) — please show me}

\label{lesson:HI-C111-dikhaie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for in Hindi, then the Hindi for how do you say it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{दिखाइए}}
\textbf{\hi{दिखाइए}} (\emph{dikhāie}) — \textquotedblleft{}please show me\textquotedblright{}.

It is built on \textbf{\hi{देखना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}: to show is to \emph{make someone see}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A request for when words run out.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dikhāie}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dikhāie}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{dikhāie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for in Hindi, then the Hindi for how do you say it, then say \emph{dikhāie} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{दिखाइए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please show me\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sunāī nahīṁ diyā]{\hi{सुनाई} \hi{नहीं} \hi{दिया} (sunāī nahīṁ diyā) — I could not hear it}

\label{lesson:HI-C111-sunai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for how do you say it, then the Hindi for please show me.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सुनाई} \hi{नहीं} \hi{दिया}}
\textbf{\hi{सुनाई} \hi{नहीं} \hi{दिया}} (\emph{sunāī nahīṁ diyā}) — \textquotedblleft{}I could not hear it\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}hearing was not given\textquotedblright{}.

It is built on \textbf{\hi{सुनना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to hear\textquotedblright{}. Pair it with a fix: \textbf{\hi{ज़ोर} \hi{से} \hi{बोलिए}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An honest reason to ask again.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sunāī nahīṁ diyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sunāī nahīṁ diyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sunāī nahīṁ diyā, zor se bolie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for how do you say it, then the Hindi for please show me, then say \emph{sunāī nahīṁ diyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सुनाई} \hi{नहीं} \hi{दिया} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}I could not hear it\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[likh dījie]{\hi{लिख} \hi{दीजिए} (likh dījie) — please write it down}

\label{lesson:HI-C111-likhdijie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for please show me, then the Hindi for I could not hear it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{लिख} \hi{दीजिए}}
\textbf{\hi{लिख} \hi{दीजिए}} (\emph{likh dījie}) — \textquotedblleft{}please write it down (for me)\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{लिखना}} is \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\hi{दीजिए}} adds \textquotedblleft{}for me\textquotedblright{}, as in \textbf{\hi{एक} \hi{चाय} \hi{दीजिए}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
In Hindi, how do you say it, show me, I could not hear, write it down.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{likh dījie}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{likh dījie}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{likh dījie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for please show me, then the Hindi for I could not hear it, then say \emph{likh dījie} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{लिख} \hi{दीजिए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please write it down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
